Job Description

We are currently seeking a Sr Level Geologist to support a wide variety of environmental projects. The preferred candidate will have extensive field experience working at Superfund and other contaminated sites, running complex field programs, preparing planning documents and preparing reports for environmental characterization and remediation projects.

As a member of this team, you would contribute to CDM Smith's mission by:

Experience supporting environmental investigations, site characterization, remediation, reclamation, or closure activities at active, inactive, or legacy mining sites.
Demonstrated knowledge of mine waste characterization, including waste rock, tailings, heap leach facilities, and acid rock drainage/acid mine drainage evaluations.
Experience conducting and overseeing drilling programs, monitoring well installation, lithologic logging, core logging, and hydrogeologic investigations.
Familiarity with collection and interpretation of groundwater, surface water, soil, sediment, waste rock, and tailings sampling data at mining facilities.
Experience evaluating metals fate and transport, geochemistry, water quality, and contaminant migration associated with mining operations.
Knowledge of federal and state environmental regulations applicable to mining projects, including CERCLA, RCRA, CWA, NEPA, and mine reclamation requirements.
Experience preparing or reviewing technical documents such as Sampling and Analysis Plans (SAPs), Quality Assurance Project Plans (QAPPs), Remedial Investigation reports, Feasibility Studies, and permit applications.
Proficiency with geologic and hydrogeologic conceptual site model development.
Experience using GIS, geologic modeling, and environmental data management software to support mine investigations and remediation projects.
Familiarity with mine closure planning, reclamation design, and long-term monitoring programs.
Experience supporting environmental compliance, permitting, and stakeholder coordination for mining projects.
Understanding of geotechnical, hydrogeologic, and geochemical factors affecting mine site stability and environmental performance.
MSHA training and experience working safely in active mining environments.

jobs.description:
Job Summary

JOB DESCRIPTION

This position is responsible for geological mapping, resource evaluation, drill program management, and subsurface modeling across surface mining operations in the East and South Divisions generally, and Florida, Georgia and South Carolina specifically. Primary responsibilities also include interpreting geological data, estimating aggregate reserves, providing technical analysis, advice, and geological support to mining operations, Division Management, and Geological Services staff.

Essential Functions

Critical Competencies

Proficient in the use of AutoCAD, Carlson Geology Software, HxGN Geology CAD, ArcGIS/QGIS, RockWorks or other Spreadsheet/Database software packages.
Plan, manage, and execute exploratory and developmental drilling programs, core logging, and rock sample collection.
Gather and utilize geological mapping, drill data, hydrologic information, quality testing results, topography, aerial photography, survey data, sales forecasts, and other geologic data to design 3-D geological and block models.
Gather, review, analyze, and document property lines, mining setbacks, easements, zoning, special use agreements, neighbor concerns, and other site-specific land use information as necessary for the geological evaluation process.
Calculate, categorize, and document aggregate reserve and resource estimates in compliance with company and industry standards.
Interpret structural, stratigraphical, and lithological features to evaluate material quality, overburden thickness, and slope stability risk.
Support short-term and long-term mine plans by identifying geological hazards, rock quality variations, structural discontinuities, and groundwater conditions.
Assist operations personnel in interpreting deposit quality, optimizing pit faces, complying with permit conditions, laws, regulations, and guidelines, and in maintaining the systems necessary for compliance.
Identify opportunities to optimize resource recovery, minimize waste rock, reduce operating costs, and reduce impacts to neighbors.
Assist in preparation of presentations, documentations, reports, cross-sections, and geological maps as needed.
Maintain aerial photos, topographic maps, drill logs, and geological spatial databases on the network server in an up-to-date and current status.
As directed, may interact with outside consultants and testing laboratories for geological projects.
Participate in zoning efforts, special projects, and property acquisitions as necessary.
Customer Service - Understands, anticipates, and meets customer needs while ensuring a positive experience and building long-term relationships.
Attention to Detail - Ability to thoroughly and accurately complete tasks; meticulous and precise when handling information, and is critical in ensuring the quality, accuracy, and integrity of the results.
Analytical Thinking - Ability to break down complex problems, situations, in order to understand underlying patterns, identify key issues; examine information logically, question assumptions, and draw conclusions based on evidence.
Communication - Communicates clearly and effectively, both verbally and in writing, while actively listening and adapting the message to the audience.
Decision Making - Makes informed, effective, and timely decisions by evaluating available information, considering potential outcomes, and choosing the best course of action; analyzes options, weighs risks and benefits, and uses sound judgment to reach decisions that align with organizational goals and values.
Product Knowledge - Understands and can explain succinctly VMC products and/or services including their composition, features, benefits, and limitations.

Responsibilities

Education

BS or MS in Geology

Experience

5+ years experience, construction aggregate industry preferred
PG preferred

Knowledge, Skills, And Abilities

Must have the ability, either through formal training or experience, to create geological models, compute stone reserves, and interpret data including geologic testing results, geophysical logs, topographic maps, and regulatory requirements. Basic surveying and GIS knowledge preferred. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills are necessary. Must have knowledge of basic geological concepts, structural geology, stratigraphy, mineralogy, as well as of the federal, state, and local regulations and statutes which affect mining operations. Proficient skills in 3D modeling, CAD design, Excel, and other computer related software are required.

Excellent interpersonal and communication skills are mandatory. Must be able to present complex geological information in a clear and concise manner. The position requires ability to successfully interact and build relationships with VMC personnel from a wide range of departments and levels of authority, as well as with representatives of government and regulatory agencies.

Behavioral Expectations:
Employees are expected to be self-motivated and to manage multiple projects effectively without close supervision. Must be able to work effectively both independently and as part of a team. Employees are expected to behave ethically and with integrity at all times. Must comply with safety and environmental rules, policies, and regulations. Strong positive customer service attitude toward internal and external customers is expected.

Other Requirements

Up to 50% travel time, sometimes requiring overnight stay.
Work environment will be both indoors in an office and outside in a quarry or vacant land. The employee will be required to sit working at a desktop computer for several hours a day while in the office. The employee will be required to walk and carry computer field equipment or survey equipment when working outside. The outside setting will expose the employee to changes in weather, temperature, and humidity and will require walking on uneven and sometimes steep ground surfaces.
May be required to climb slopes, stoop, bend, squat, kneel, crawl or reach above shoulders to accomplish functions of the job.
Position will require ability to operate a motor vehicle within a quarry area as well as on the open road, which would require the use of both hands and feet.

Position Introduction

Join the Carl Albert Center at the University of Oklahoma as the Project Coordinator for a two-year project funded by the National Endowment for the Humanities. The project, Constitutional Foundations Archive, will digitize and make available over 30,000 previously inaccessible documents, photographs, personal papers, and audio files that illustrate the establishment and expansion of federal institutions, state constitutional development, and the evolution of congressional representation in America. Our project will focus on Oklahoma Statehood, the Oklahoma Constitution, attempts to amend the U.S. Constitution and important legislation.

This position will implement the work plan created by the PI and Co-PI, supervise undergraduate hourly and graduate student workers, coordinate activities related to the project, establish, and maintain on-going reporting process. The ideal candidate will have a masters degree in library or archives science and have experience implementing large archival projects.

What You'll Do

As a Data Analyst II, you will be a key analytics partner on a cross‑functional product team comprised of Data Engineering, Data Analytics, and Product Management. In this role, you will develop insights through general analytics and statistical modeling, examine and identify data patterns and trends, and deliver presentations or dashboards that support data-driven storytelling and business decisions.

Beginner/Intermediate Data Preparation: Utilizes best practices in data preparation, data quality, analytics, and dashboard design to provide business partners with trusted and actionable insights.
Beginner/Intermediate Modeling Skills: Performs statistical modeling on existing data sets. Develop analytic models that support business initiatives. Effectively utilize sophisticated tools/technologies to mine data sources providing relevant information in a consumable manner. Familiar with common statistical methods and applications (A/B testing, probability, regression).
Examines and identifies data patterns and trends to help answer business questions, provide insights, and improve data-driven decision making.
Beginner/Intermediate Decision Making and Critical Thinking: Consulting with our business partners to use the data available to investigate issues facing the business, without always having a well-defined hypothesis. Understanding of the issues related to the decision-making process; ability to analyze situations fully and accurately, and reach productive decisions.
Beginner/Intermediate Visualization Skills: Able to effectively articulate insights to help stakeholders answer the most critical questions. Create compelling written, numeric and visual summaries.

Design, build, maintain, and continuously improve analytics products, dashboards, and reporting solutions aligned to business and product objectives.
Partner with data engineers and fellow analysts throughout the analytics lifecycle to source, validate, interpret, and communicate data that supports business decisions.

Bachelor's degree in a Business, Technical, or Analytical field (e.g., Data Analytics, Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, Finance, Economics, or related field).
